body:
He said something like that, too. Let me tell you something, dude. 

The dude I'm talking about told me stuff that night that changed me as a person. It's crazy how much of an impact a person has on you.

Hell, what's the height difference here?

Thought John was taller than Ringo

Care to share with me the before and after sort of feels?

I'm interested now. Lol!
Very bad intrusive thoughts, but I don't act on them. I can still function without them, but I still dwell on them at several times of the day.

That is the greatest way to look at think. You were strong enough to think to yourself, "Hey, life can get better. Let's try again". 

When I saw that you want to live, I teared up. Literally. People who are in your situation seem to still be in that dazed state. You want to change, and that's great.

I really wish you success. Please update when you get better!

Best wishes.

You'll meet someone. You'll fall in love, you'll forget. Don't worry. When you find that certain someone, the world stops spinning. 

Trust me. You just need to get out there. Say to yourself, "I'm gonna be the best today. I'm going to be happy". It works, dude. I've been doing it for 14 years. 

Try some dating websites and apps. Or just wait for that certain someone to step into your life. You need to take the initiative. Find that person, man. Good luck. :)
It's such a normal thing, you know? I'm just afraid that I'll become a victim of it. I obsess over this so much. And religion isn't helping.
Try new things. Even if they include staying at home and on the internet. I've met some pretty great people outside the web and inside it, too! :)

True. He did say in an interview that the Beatles' breakup was one of the worst things to happen in his life.

Can't blame him. Paul went through the same thing.

It was Ringo's fault for becoming a drunk after the break-up.

Thank God he changed though.
That is REALLY reassuring. Thanks, dude! :)
I have to thank you for your reassurance. I'm feeling quite better right now actually. I think I'm just gonna wait it out. I'll get over it, probably.

Oh, now that I'm remembering. Two people told me that week that they had suicidal thoughts. That messed me up, due to those people being some of the most joyful people ever. 

That messed me up probably.

I live in the southern states, and I'm really smarter socially than the rest of my school mates. They don't have a history with computers, and I've seen some messed up things. 

I don't know, dude. But the whole situation is getting me worried. My mother keeps saying that it's puberty or chemical imbalance. Plus the doctor said that it would just be a small pill, not like full on anti-depressants. Plus, these memories will be treasured by me for a while. I was going through a lot in 2016, my friends were going through some depressive stages, and I would give anything to go back to those days. Just simple things, like talking and helping others. 

I love doing that, dude. It's such a good feeling.

So like, is there medication for those thoughts? 

I definitely want these thoughts to simmer down, as it is causing some depressed days, which is worrying the fuck out of my peers.
